msg: This line installs the ultralytics package, which is AGPL-3.0. Ultralytics: "An Enterprise License is required if you want to use Ultralytics YOLO without open-sourcing your entire project", and that includes internal business tools, SaaS back ends and edge devices.
fix: rfdetr  (Apache-2.0 for Nano, Small, Medium and Large)

msg: The yolov5 pip package repackages Ultralytics YOLOv5 code, which Ultralytics publishes under AGPL-3.0. The Ultralytics Enterprise License covers "the complete Ultralytics YOLO source code portfolio, including YOLO26, earlier YOLO versions", so YOLOv5 is not exempt.

The ultralytics/* base image ships the AGPL-3.0 ultralytics package in every container built from it, including containers deployed to cameras, robots and edge devices, which Ultralytics lists as needing an Enterprise License.
fix: FROM python:3.12-slim  +  RUN pip install --no-cache-dir rfdetr

msg: This line pulls Ultralytics YOLO source straight from GitHub. The code carries the same AGPL-3.0 terms as the pip package, so a vendored copy needs an Enterprise License or a fully published project.
fix: pip install rfdetr  (drop the cloned repo)

msg: torch.hub.load downloads and runs the AGPL-3.0 Ultralytics repository at runtime, so the service uses Ultralytics YOLO even though no requirements file lists it.
fix: from rfdetr import RFDETRMedium; model = RFDETRMedium()

msg: Python code that imports ultralytics is part of the derivative work the AGPL-3.0 terms reach. Swap the import when the dependency goes.

Pretrained Ultralytics YOLO weights. The Enterprise License lists the pretrained models among what it covers, so shipping or downloading these weights in a closed product is part of the licence question too.
fix: RFDETRMedium()  (Apache-2.0 weights for Nano to Large)

msg: The yolo command is the Ultralytics command-line tool, installed by the ultralytics package. Build steps and scripts that call it keep the AGPL-3.0 package in the image.
Already on RF-DETR, but this size is not Apache-2.0: the XL and 2XL detection models and the rfdetr_plus extension are under PML 1.0. Nano, Small, Medium and Large are Apache-2.0.
